exercise.name: Cable Kneeling Pulldown

reference.title: Cable Kneeling Pulldown (version 3)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder adduction and extension, scapular depression, elbow flexion)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the bar comes down to the chest, breathe in as it rises.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, short pause, about 2 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can pull to the upper chest without swinging back.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack

cues.text: Kneel tall on a mat facing a high pulley, knees hip width, hips over the knees; hold the lat bar overhand a little wider than the shoulders, arms long reaching up.
Breathe out; draw the shoulder blades down and pull the bar in front of the face to the upper chest, elbows down and back.
Bar at the upper chest, ribs down, glutes tight so the hips stay over the knees.
Breathe in and let the bar rise under control until the arms are long.
Full stretch at the top without arching the lower back, then pull again.

mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and keep the hips over the knees.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the lower back as the bar comes down
mistakes.fix: Keep the ribs down and the trunk still.
Lead each rep with the shoulder blades down.

mistakes.mistake: Kneeling so close that the cable runs into the face
mistakes.fix: Kneel back so the bar comes down in front of the face.

kinematics.setup: Overhand, 52 cm between the hands on a 120 cm lat bar (shoulders 40 cm apart)
kinematics.norm: Overhand, a little wider than the shoulders; grip width changes lat activation little (Lusk 2010, Signorile 2002)
From nearly straight to about 100-120 degrees (clinical opinion)
From overhead to the upper arms beside the trunk (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Tall kneeling, ≈7° back of vertical, knees 20.8 cm apart
kinematics.norm: Tall kneeling with a small lean back from the knees (clinical opinion; Lehman 2004 lat pulldown variations)

kinematics.peak: 1.2 s down, 0.4 s at the chest, 2 s up
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 1 s down and 2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Kneeling Pulldown (version 3), video (movement reference)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)
Signorile, Zink & Szwed 2002, a comparative electromyographical investigation of muscle utilization patterns using various hand positions during the lat pull-down (J Strength Cond Res 16(4):539-546)
Lusk, Hale and Russell 2010, grip width and forearm orientation effects on muscle activity during the lat pull-down (J Strength Cond Res 24(7):1895-1900)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can move with the trunk still and the shoulders down.
Kneel on a mat; let the bar back up before standing.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee discomfort: kneel on a thicker pad or use a seated pulldown.
Shoulder discomfort overhead: stop the bar a little lower at the top.
